records.title: Pitch Diameter
records.engineering_summary: Primary functional diameter controlling thread fit behavior.
records.definition: Diameter where thread ridge and groove widths are equal, commonly used as the functional fit control dimension.

records.title: Major Diameter
records.engineering_summary: Largest diameter of a thread profile used in nominal designation.
records.definition: Maximum diameter measured at thread crest for external threads or thread root envelope for internal profiles.

records.title: Minor Diameter
records.engineering_summary: Smallest diameter associated with thread roots.
records.definition: Minimum thread diameter measured near root geometry and used for strength and engagement interpretation.

records.title: Allowance
records.engineering_summary: Intentional dimensional difference used to establish fit baseline.
records.definition: Planned offset between mating parts that sets nominal clearance or interference before manufacturing variation is applied.

records.title: Tolerance Zone
records.engineering_summary: Range location and width controlling allowable variation around nominal form.
records.definition: Bounded dimensional range assigned by class notation that defines permissible manufacturing variation for a thread element.

records.title: Thread Pitch
records.engineering_summary: Axial distance between adjacent thread forms.
records.definition: Linear distance measured parallel to thread axis between corresponding points on adjacent thread profiles.

records.title: ISO 965 Tolerance System
records.engineering_summary: ISO tolerance class framework for metric screw threads.
records.definition: Concept entity linking metric thread fit class interpretation to the ISO 965 standards family.

records.title: Fit Class 6H
records.engineering_summary: Common internal metric thread class in general engineering use.
records.definition: Internal metric thread class notation used in ISO system with class grade and zone designation.

records.title: Fit Class 6g
records.engineering_summary: Common external metric thread class in general engineering use.
records.definition: External metric thread class notation used in ISO system with class grade and zone designation.

records.title: UNC Thread System
records.engineering_summary: Unified inch coarse thread system used broadly in imperial fastener ecosystems.
records.definition: Unified coarse thread series defined in inch units and organized by nominal diameter and threads per inch.

records.title: Taper Tap
records.engineering_summary: Tap style with a long chamfer that engages several threads gradually before reaching full diameter.
records.definition: A tap with a gradually tapered chamfer at the point, typically engaging six to eight threads before reaching full thread form, used to start threads gradually and reduce cutting force per pass.

application_notes.fact: Chamfer length is approximately 7-10 threads/pitches, the longest of the three chamfer-length tap styles.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources (Travers Tool, MisolTap, Rapmaf, AIMS Industrial)

application_notes.fact: Long chamfer distributes cutting load gradually and makes the tap easier to start straight/square, but it cannot cut full-depth threads within roughly 7-10 pitches of the bottom of a blind hole.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

records.title: Plug Tap
records.engineering_summary: Tap style with a moderate chamfer length between taper and bottoming taps.
records.definition: A tap with a moderate chamfer length, shorter than a taper tap but longer than a bottoming tap, engaging approximately three to five threads before reaching full thread form.

application_notes.fact: Chamfer length is approximately 3-5 threads/pitches, shorter than a taper tap and longer than a bottoming tap.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

application_notes.fact: General-purpose tap; commonly the sole tap used for through-hole tapping, and can start in an unthreaded hole (unlike a bottoming tap).
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

records.title: Bottoming Tap
records.engineering_summary: Tap style with a very short chamfer for threading close to the bottom of a blind hole.
records.definition: A tap with a short chamfer, typically engaging one to one and a half threads before reaching full thread form, designed to cut threads as close as practical to the bottom of a blind hole.

application_notes.fact: Chamfer length is approximately 1-2 threads/pitches, the shortest of the three chamfer-length tap styles.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

application_notes.fact: Cannot start in an unthreaded hole; used to extend threads to the base of a blind hole after a taper and/or plug tap has already established the thread.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

application_notes.fact: Incomplete internal threads are inherently present at the bottom of a tapped blind hole -- the physical reason bottoming taps exist as a distinct style.
application_notes.source: NASA-STD-5020A section 4.7.5 [TFSR 25]: "Where blind holes are tapped, incomplete internal threads are present at the bottom of the hole."

records.title: Spiral Point Tap
records.engineering_summary: Tap style with an angled point geometry that directs chips ahead of the tap.
records.definition: A tap with an angled point ground onto the flutes that pushes chips forward, ahead of the tap and out through the far side of the hole, commonly associated with through-hole applications.

application_notes.fact: Also called a gun tap or gun-nose tap; a forward-angled point ground onto the cutting chamfer drives chips forward, ahead of the tap.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources (Cutwel, MisolTap, Slugger Tools)

application_notes.fact: Suited to through-hole tapping only. In a blind hole the forward-pushed chips have nowhere to go, pack at the bottom, and can bind and break the tap.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources; consistent with NASA-STD-5020A's confirmation that blind-hole tapped threads terminate at a closed bottom with no chip escape path

records.title: Spiral Flute Tap
records.engineering_summary: Tap style with helical flutes that direct chips back out of the hole entrance.
records.definition: A tap with helical (spiral) flutes that lift chips backward out of the hole entrance during cutting, commonly associated with blind-hole applications.

application_notes.fact: Helical (spiral) flutes lift chips backward, up and out of the hole entrance, opposite in direction to a spiral-point tap.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

application_notes.fact: Suited to blind-hole tapping, where chips cannot be pushed forward out of a closed bottom.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

records.title: Forming Tap
records.engineering_summary: Tap style that displaces material to form threads rather than cutting them.
records.definition: A tap that forms threads by radially displacing material rather than cutting it, producing no chips; also referred to as a roll tap or fluteless tap.

application_notes.fact: Requires a ductile workpiece material -- commonly cited minimum elongation of roughly 8% and maximum hardness of roughly Rc 30 -- because threads are formed by plastic displacement, not cutting.
application_notes.source: Commonly cited across manufacturer/tooling technical guides (e.g. Harvey Performance, Jarvis Cutting Tools); not independently verified against a primary standard in this phase

application_notes.fact: Unsuitable for brittle materials such as cast iron, which can crack rather than flow under the forming pressure.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple manufacturer technical guides

application_notes.fact: Requires a larger pre-tap hole diameter than an equivalent cutting tap, since material is displaced outward rather than removed.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple manufacturer technical guides

application_notes.fact: Produces no chips, which removes chip-evacuation as a constraint on blind-hole use -- unlike cutting taps, hole geometry (blind vs. through) is not the limiting factor for this tap type; material ductility is.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple manufacturer technical guides

records.title: Hand Tap
records.engineering_summary: General term for a tap intended for manual operation, often supplied as a set.
records.definition: A tap designed for manual operation with a tap wrench, typically supplied as part of a set spanning taper, plug, and bottoming chamfer styles for a given thread size.

application_notes.fact: Designed for manual operation with a tap wrench; commonly supplied as a taper/plug/bottoming set for progressive blind-hole tapping by hand.
application_notes.source: Cross-corroborated across multiple machining reference sources

records.title: Pilot Hole
records.engineering_summary: A hole drilled before a thread-forming or thread-cutting operation.
records.definition: A hole drilled prior to tapping, sized to leave the appropriate amount of material for a tap to engage and form or cut internal threads.

records.title: Through Hole
records.engineering_summary: A hole that passes completely through a workpiece.
records.definition: A hole that passes completely through a workpiece, open at both ends, as distinct from a blind hole.

records.title: Blind Hole
records.engineering_summary: A hole that does not pass completely through a workpiece.
records.definition: A hole that terminates within a workpiece rather than passing all the way through, closed at one end.

records.title: Tapped Hole
records.engineering_summary: A hole in which internal threads have been cut or formed.
records.definition: A hole in which internal threads have been cut or formed, ready to accept a mating externally threaded fastener.

records.title: Clearance Hole
records.engineering_summary: A hole sized larger than a fastener's threads so the fastener passes through without engaging.
records.definition: A hole sized larger than a fastener's major diameter so the fastener body passes through freely without thread engagement, typically paired with a nut or a tapped hole in a mating part.

records.title: Cut Tapping
records.engineering_summary: A tapping operation in which material is removed to form threads.
records.definition: A tapping operation in which a cutting-style tap removes material to form internal threads, producing chips.

records.title: Form Tapping
records.engineering_summary: A tapping operation in which material is displaced rather than removed to form threads.
records.definition: A tapping operation in which a forming (roll) tap displaces material radially to create internal threads without removing material or producing chips.
